meta.title: Routes
meta.description: The 36 route maps that adventure paths are built from: the ROGUE_ROUTE naming scheme, the six terrain types, each route's three-type wild table, forest/cave item drop rarity bonuses, the calm/average/tough route sub-types, and the six FAIRY typing swaps EX makes. The route table itself is byte-identical between Vanilla and EX — all 36 routes (including Sinnoh's) exist in both versions.

prose.heading: The route naming scheme
prose.text: Every route is its own dedicated map with the name ROGUE_ROUTE_<Region>_<Type><N>. Hoenn routes carry no region prefix (ROGUE_ROUTE_FIELD0, ROGUE_ROUTE_CAVE0, ROGUE_ROUTE_MOUNTAIN1…), while Kanto, Johto and Sinnoh routes are prefixed (ROGUE_ROUTE_KANTO_FIELD0, ROGUE_ROUTE_JOHTO_CAVE0, ROGUE_ROUTE_SINNOH_201). Sinnoh routes use the region's real route numbers — 201, 205, 207, 209, 210, 212, 214, 215, 217 — plus three named locations: EternaForest, MtCoronet and IronIsland. The table is identical between the Vanilla and EX versions — all 36 routes, including Sinnoh's, exist in both; the only branch difference in the file is the wild type table of six routes (EX swaps one type to Fairy) and the legendary encounter table that lives in the same header.

prose.heading: Route types and wild Pokémon
prose.text: Each route carries a wild type table of exactly three types (for example, Hoenn Forest 0: Bug, Ghost, Poison) — a pool the encounters draw from, not a roster you can count on. When a route room is placed, the game builds a candidate pool of non-legendary species matching any of those three types (directly, or through an evolution), then fills the grass encounter table from it (5 slots on Calm routes, 3 on Average, 2 on Tough — wild-encounter Charms and Curses can add or subtract slots). The first slot is reserved for the room's hint type — one of the table's three, cycled by the room's position on the path board — so if the pool has a species of that type the slot is guaranteed to be it, and if not it falls back to a random pool species, while the remaining slots fill with other random species from the same pool. The battle you actually face draws a random slot from the table (recent repeats are skipped), so the hint type biases the table but never guarantees a particular encounter. Water encounters (2 on Calm, 1 on Average and Tough) are separate: they come from a Water-type-only table fixed at the start of the run, never from the route's three types. Those same three types also drive the route's themed weather: the sub-type's weather roll (5%, 25% or 45% — never rolled at the first ladder stage, before your first badge) picks one of the three types at random, and only types with a weather (Normal, Flying and Dragon have none) change it. Each route can also define an item drop rarity bonus, which is added to every item drop it makes — forests and caves are therefore the best routes for item hunting.

prose.heading: Calm, Average and Tough routes
prose.text: Every Route room on a generated path rolls a difficulty sub-type — calm, average or tough — and the sub-type tunes what the route offers, from encounter counts and trainer spawns to item drops and themed weather (what the roll does with the chosen type is in the Route types section above). The roll itself shifts late in the run: from difficulty 9, the second Elite Four path, tough routes dominate.

roll.phase: Difficulty 9+ (from the second Elite Four path)

prose.heading: How routes appear on the adventure path
prose.text: A Route room is one of the 16 room types a generated adventure path can contain, alongside rest stops, team hideouts, honey trees, labs, shrines, signs and the final boss room. When a Route room is placed, the game picks a route from the full 36-route table with a weighted roll whose eligibility rotates per run: each route is assigned one of three delay-seed groups from the run's random base seed and the route's own id (so which routes land in which group changes every run), and for the current ladder stage only routes in the group matching that stage (the stage count modulo three) are eligible — a pacing rule that brings different route groups into play as the ladder climbs (if none of the unplaced routes match, every unplaced route becomes eligible again as a fallback). Repetition is handled separately: an 18-slot history buffer remembers every route already placed on the current path, and those routes get zero weight, so the same route can never appear twice on one path. The room's warp then leads into the chosen route map. A route's region flag also sets its battle music: Kanto routes play Red/Green (Gen 1) tracks, Johto routes HeartGold/SoulSilver-style, Sinnoh routes Diamond/Pearl-style, and Hoenn routes keep the default Emerald themes.
